title: Device hardening
goal_html: Students apply a device-hardening checklist to a fictional device configuration, identify which controls are missing, and justify each finding using the principle of least privilege and attack surface reduction. Ties to LO 4.3.A (explain and apply hardening controls).
steps_html:
1. Each pair opens the simulation and works through the device-configuration scenarios. Before submitting each answer they must agree and write one sentence explaining why that control reduces risk.
  2. After the simulation, each pair reviews the configuration card below and identifies which of the five hardening controls the fictional device fails. They record their findings in a table: Control | Pass/Fail | Reason.
  3. Pairs swap their findings table with another pair, who must either agree or rebut each finding with a justification.

Fictional device configuration card (Meridian Technologies, Workstation WS-04)

OS: Windows 10 (installed 18 months ago, no updates applied)
Local accounts: Administrator (password: admin), Guest (enabled, password: none)
Services running: FTP server, Telnet, Remote Desktop, HTTP server, Print spooler
Firewall: disabled
Disk encryption: off
Screen lock timeout: never
collaborate_html: Assign roles: one partner is the "security auditor" (identifies failures and writes the finding), the other is the "device owner" (tries to justify why the current setting might seem reasonable). The auditor must respond to each defense with a concrete attack scenario that the control would prevent. Swap roles after finding three issues.
exit_html: Each student submits a ranked list of the three most critical controls the fictional device is missing, with one sentence each explaining the specific risk that control addresses.
